details.label: INCORRECT
details.reasoning: The question says the sampled variables themselves become normally distributed as the number of samples increases. The Central Limit Theorem concerns the distribution of the sample mean, not the original sampled variables, so naming it as the supporting theory contradicts the gold target.
details.groundedness_reasoning:
1. The gold target says no theory supports the statement as phrased.
2. Citation [3] limits the Central Limit Theorem to the sampling distribution of a sample mean, rather than the distribution of the sampled variables themselves.
3. Citation [6] distinguishes the i.i.d. variables, which share the same distribution, from a normalized sample mean, whose distribution converges to normality.
4. Together, these passages support the distinction needed to derive that the stated claim about the sampled variables themselves is not what the Central Limit Theorem says.
